text: The new medication seems to be helping. Two good days in a row. Not getting carried away, but this feels like a door opening.
Second interview next week. They said I'm one of three. I let myself imagine saying yes.
First green shoots on the plot after the long winter. Maybe this year the garden will actually work.
Sat down with Rahel and made a budget we can actually stick to. For the first time I can see us getting out of debt.
Dad said he'll try the support group. It's a small step. It's the biggest step he's taken in years.
Things are still hard but I can see a way through now. That's new.
The surgeon thinks the second operation has a good chance. Holding on to the word 'good'.
Valentina and I talked properly last night for the first time since the fight. I think we're going to be okay.
Filled in the application for the art foundation course. Whatever happens, I tried.
Three weeks without a panic attack. I'm starting to believe I can get better.
The ceasefire is holding. Called my cousins back home and for once they sounded light.
New year, clean notebook. I have a feeling this one will be kinder.
IVF round three starts next month. Dr. Salazar is optimistic. Trying to be too.
Spoke to a lawyer about the visa. There might be a route after all.
Lena called from rehab. She sounded clearer than I've heard her in two years.
Signed the lease on a small studio for the business. It's tiny. It's a start.
Sun came out after nine days of rain and I felt something lift. Maybe spring is actually coming.
My son spoke two full sentences to his speech therapist today. She says he's ready for the next stage.
Not where I want to be yet but closer than last year. Holding onto that.
The council finally agreed to look at the crossing outside the school. Maybe the petition worked.
Pavel wrote back. Short message, but friendly. Maybe the friendship isn't over after all.
Started a savings jar for the trip. Only £40 so far but I can see it now.
Bloodwork is improving. Numbers going the right direction for the first time since diagnosis.
Bad week, but I'm going to bed thinking tomorrow could be different. That's something.
My first therapy session was awkward and I cried the whole time. But Anja, the therapist, said 'we can work with this' and I believed her.
The adoption agency called. We've moved up the list.
I think I'm ready to date again. Not rushing. Just open.
Marisol got the job interview she wanted. Helping her prepare. Feels like her luck is turning.
Kids planted sunflowers along the fence. They're asking every day if they've grown. We'll see in summer.
Mum's scan shows the tumour has shrunk. Long road still. But shrunk.
After months of no response, two companies want to talk next week. Something's moving.
Wrote one page today after six months of nothing. Maybe the writing is coming back.
The new teacher, Mr. Okonkwo, seems to really get my daughter. Fingers crossed this year is easier for her.
I keep picturing the little house by the sea. One day. Saving towards it.
Physio says I might be walking without the frame by Christmas.
I had a real laugh today for the first time since Maya passed. It felt like a sign that life goes on.
The company is restructuring but my manager says my role looks safe. Trying to trust that.
Joined the climate group in town. Twenty people in a church hall with a plan. Felt like maybe we can do something.
Tobias and I are trying counselling. First session was rocky but we both stayed in the room.
Got a good mark on the mock. Maybe I'm not as behind as I thought.
There's a waiting list for the specialist but at least I'm on it now. Progress.
Our offer went in on the flat. We find out Friday. Already picturing the window seat.
Today I didn't feel better but I believed I would eventually. That's enough for today.
Ahmad is out of intensive care. Moving to the general ward tomorrow.
Planted the apple tree for the grandchildren I might have one day.
My sister reached out after three years of silence. Just 'hi, can we talk?'. I said yes.
Feeling optimistic about the new year at work. New team lead, Fatima, seems great.
The rescue dog let me pet her today. Took six weeks. She's learning that hands can be gentle.
Exam board accepted my appeal. I get to resit in summer.
Hopeful, tentatively. The test was negative but they want a follow-up in March.
Someone at the meeting shared their story of recovery and I thought: that could be me in two years.
The first article I pitched got accepted. One acceptance. That's how it starts.
I'm learning to cook properly. Tonight's dal was edible! There's hope for me yet.
Gus is walking a little further every day since the stroke. Today to the end of the garden.
Brighter week. Starting to think the worst might be behind us.
I wrote down where I want to be in five years and for once it didn't feel like fantasy.
The landlord might sell to us rather than to a developer. Meeting him Thursday.
Every small step counts, Ingrid keeps telling me. Today I believed her.
Our town's library is reopening thanks to the volunteers. Signed up to help on Saturdays.
Grief is still here but it's softer this month. I can see a future with joy in it.
The clinic called back. There's a trial I might qualify for.
Moved the last box into the new place. It's empty and echoing and full of possibility.
Talked to Wei about the business idea and she wants in. With two of us it might actually work.
My hands are steadier this week. The tremor clinic said that's a good sign.
Maybe I'm allowed to want more. Writing that here before I talk myself out of it.
Kids and I made a vision board for the summer: beach, picnics, bikes. Looking forward to every square of it.
Interview went well. Panel smiled a lot. Trying not to read into it. Reading into it.
Baba agreed to move in with us. It'll be tight but we'll take care of him properly now.
The crack in the ceiling turned out to be cosmetic. The house isn't falling down. Maybe we can stay after all.
I think next year is going to be good. Just a feeling. Writing it down so I can check.
